Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Writ Petition No. 12365 Of 2022
O R D E R:

This Writ Petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" .... to issue an appropriate writ or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondent No.5 in unlawful interference in running petitioner's business in the name and style of M/s Blue Bottle Coffee Shop at Madhapur, Hyderabad as unlawful, arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 19(1) (g) of the Constitution of India..."

2. Dr. J. Vijayalakshmi, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has a licence to carry out the business of running the coffee shop / restaurant and as a part of the business, the petitioner also offers hookah pot to the customers subject to satisfaction that the visiting customers are above 18 years of age, by taking a photocopy of the proof as evidence to that effect.
It is submitted that the petitioner had obtained appropriate trade licenses from competent authority.
It is also submitted that pursuant to the directions of the Apex Court, separate smoking area has been earmarked in the coffee shop exclusively for smoking hookah.

Learned counsel submits that as per Section 4 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, the petitioner restaurant has seating capacity of more than 30 persons, hence, a separate provision for smoking area is provided.

sentences.text: He submits that the 5th respondent is frequently interfering with the business activity of serving hookah in the designated smoking area in the restaurant and preventing the petitioner from doing trade.

It is also submitted that the action of the respondents in asking them to stop offering hookah in the absence of any material to show that the business is in violation of the guidelines prescribed by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal No. 10836 of 2014 arising out of SLP (Civil)
No. 30832 of 2011 in Narinder S. Chadha v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai and the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution Act, 2003 (for short, 'the Act') amounts to infringement of fundamental rights and the same is illegal and improper.

sentences.text: This Court has all the concern for the protection of the health of the adolescents falling prey to this menace of smoking tobacco products in whatever form, but so long as tobacco products, which includes hookah tobacco and consumption thereof is permitted in smoking zone as per the provision to Section 4 of the Act, use of such a tobacco product by persons above the age of 18 years, in a space provided for that purpose cannot be stopped unless and until the law circumscribes and prohibits such consumption of hookah tobacco in the smoking zones."

Learned counsel submits that the respondents cannot interfere with the business of the petitioner in view of the law laid down by this Court which was fortified by the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder S Chadha's case (supra).
3.

Learned Government Pleader for Home Sri Srikanth Reddy submits that under the shadow of enabling proviso to Section 4 of the Act which says that a specific place for smokers may be provided, most of them is converting the nature of such restaurants as a place for the purpose of hookah only while allowing the youngsters to smoke hookah.
If the restaurants are converted as a place for the purpose of smoking hookah, certainly licensing authority and the police have ample power to enquire into the same.

It is stated that contrary to the purpose of running restaurants, if the persons are allowed only for the purpose of smoking hookah in the restaurants, the respondents have a right to cancel the licence also.

It is submitted that the petitioner cannot serve hookah in the restaurants without complying with the provisions of the Act and the Rules and without displaying statutory and pictorial warnings and notices, and it amounts to violation as pointed out by the police.

Further, it is stated that as per the provisions of Section 12 of the COTP Act which confers powers to the police not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police or any officer of the State Food or Drug Administration or any other officer, holding the equivalent rank being not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police authorised by the Central Government or by the State Government, may, if he has any reason to suspect that any provision of this Act has been or is being contravened, enter and search in the manner prescribed at any reasonable time at factory, building, business or any other place.

It is stated that tobacco is one of the major public health hazards and it is responsible directly or indirectly for an estimated 8 lakh deaths annually in the country and also the treatment of tobacco- related diseases and their loss of productivity cause the country much more than all the benefits recurring in the form of revenue and employment generated by tobacco industry.

sentences.text: It is stated that basing on the recommendation made by the Parliamentary Committee, a Bill was introduced in the Parliament for a comprehensive legislation to prohibit advertising and regulation of production, supply and distribution of cigarettes and tobacco products.

It is stated that as per Section 4, generally smoking in public places is prohibited, provided that in a hotel having 30 rooms or a restaurant having seating capacity of 30 persons are more and in the airports a separate provision for smoking area or space may be made.

It is stated that there is a prohibition under Section 6 of the Act on sale of cigarette or other tobacco products to a person below the age of 18 years and Section 7 restricts trade and commerce in and production, supply and distribution of,
cigarettes and other tobacco products.
It is also stated that under Section 12, police have power to enter and search and under Section 13, the police have power to seize.
It is stated that Section 29 protects the action taken by the officers in good faith.

It is submitted by the learned Government Pleader that it is the bounden duty of the police to curb illegal activities, otherwise there is every chance of spoiling the bright career of the adolescent students / youth including young girls by falling prey to drug addiction.
It is submitted that no instructions or circulars whatsoever were issued by the 2nd respondent regarding closure of hookah business in Hyderabad city.
It is submitted that whenever the respondent police received any information regarding unlawful activities in hookah centres, the respondents are visiting the centres.

Learned Government Pleader submits that as per Sections 21 and 76 of the City Police Act,
the police are filing petty case charge sheets before the Court concerned.

He submits that in Writ Petition No. 14192 of 2011 and batch, dated 01.07.2015, while disposing of the Writ Petition, this Court has observed as under:
" The police authorities would be at liberty to regulate the business undertaken by the petitioners relating to serving of flavoured hookahs in their establishments.

In terms of such regulation, it would be open to the police authorities to enter upon and cause inspection of the petitioners' business establishments for the purpose of securing due compliance with the guidelines already prescribed and also guidelines that may be prescribed in future in this regard."
Learned Government Pleader submits that the petitioner is relying on the order passed by this Court in Writ Petition No. 25439 of 2018.

He submits that even as per the orders passed by this Court in several Writ Petitions, the police authorities will be at liberty to regulate the business undertaken by the persons who are running Hookah parlours relating to serving fortified hookah in their establishment.

In view of the same, it is always open to the police authorities to cause inspection of the business establishments for the purpose of securing true compliance of the guidelines already prescribed and the guidelines to be prescribed in future.

He submits that as and when police receive any information with regard to any activity that has to been carried out in hookah parlours, contrary to the guidelines issued, it is always open to the police to inspect the premises that the respondents cannot claim it to be interference with their business.
He submits that most of the school and college-going children are visiting hookah parlours and they are becoming drug addicts.
He further submits that a duty is cast upon the police department to monitor these activities.

Hence, he submits that only in the interest of the public at large, the police have been monitoring the same and at any cost, it cannot be termed as 'interference'.

sentences.text: 4. Having heard learned counsel on either side, perused the material available on record.
5. There cannot be any dispute with regard to the fact that police have the power to regulate smoking in a public place in the manner specified as provided under Section 4 & 12 of the Act.
In some cases, the owners of the restaurants contend that they have licence from GHMC.
Though they have a trade licence from GHMC, ultimately, as per the power conferred under the Act, it is the respective police who have the authority to regulate and monitor.

Further, the object of the Act is to prohibit consumption of cigarette and other tobacco products which are injurious to health and in the larger interest of improving the public health, as per Article 47 of the Constitution of India which deals with the duty of the State to protect the public health.

It is also observed that most of the restaurants which obtained trade licence for the purpose of running a restaurant or cafeteria are converting the same into hookah parlours for running hookah centres.

As per Section 4 of the Act, a separate place is required to be maintained for restaurants which have the capacity of 30 seats, that ipso facto will not give any right to the restaurant owners to run the hookah parlours.

At the place of smoking, except smoking, no other service shall be allowed and if basing on the permission granted for a restaurant, they are only running hookah centres, the authorities have a right to cancel the licence.

Invariably, the police have to have constant check and control whether the concerned are following the provisions of the Act and the Rules and whether they are displaying statutory and pictorial warning notices.

As per Section 12 of the COTP Act, the police not below the rank of Sub-Inspector or any officer of State Food or Drug Administration or any other officer, holding the equivalent rank being not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police, authorised by the Central Government or by the State Government can inspect any building.
In view of the same, there cannot be any direction from this Court to the respondents not to visit hookah centres of the petitioner.
It has come to light that under the guise of hookah parlour, in some cases, they are getting the customers used to the other narcotic drugs.
Even on that ground also, there should be constant surveillance and check by the police.

There should be a fine balance from the respondent police where they can only interfere in the business when there is a statutory violation or any incidents that are contrary to law are taking place in the said premises, but under the guise of it, the police just like that cannot harass the persons who are running the hookah centres.
If there is any high-handed action on the part of the officer, the same can be brought to the notice of the higher authorities and the higher authorities shall take appropriate action.

The petitioner shall earmark exclusively a separate area with appropriate enclosure in the hotel premises and no other area or portion of the premises shall be used by the customers of the petitioner for smoking hookah.

6. Though the Act does not contemplate any licence to be taken, in the larger interest of the youngsters, who are visiting the hookah centres, the restaurant owners shall have a definite place for hookah / smoking.

The restaurant owners, who are having a separate place for smokiong and for hookah consumption, shall inform the same to the Station House Officer, so that they can have surveillance on the activities that are taking place in the said place and whether the business is carried out as per the norms and the procedure laid down under the Act.
Police under the guise of this, shall not harass the persons running these centers without following the procedure.
The officers, who are competent alone can enter the premises.

If there is any high-handed action on the part of the police, the same shall be brought to the notice of the higher authoirities and they shall casue enquiry into the same and take appropriate action.
